To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) bromophenyls prefer to attach to metallic nanotubes; (b) the activation energy of grafting is not significantly diameter dependent; (c) the binding energy of pairs is diameter dependent, and (d) the binding energy is significantly larger for semiconducting than for metallic nanotubes.

(i) the activation energy for bromophenyl grafting is the same for all semiconducting chiralities within numerical accuracy, which explains the experimental lack of diameter selectivity, and (ii) the binding energy of bromophenol pairs on nanotubes is proportional to 1/R( 2), where R is the nanoradius, and is favoured by only 0.05 eV with respect to the binding energies of separate moieties on metallic nanot

the functionalization is thermodynamically more favourable on metallic nanotubes than on semiconductors; that the activation energy is similar for all zigzag nanotubes; that the binding energy of the second bromophenol is smaller for wider nanotubes and that the formation of bromophenol pairs is not favoured on metallic nanotube.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the thermodynamics of the bromophenyl-functionalization of carbon nanomaterials, and it provides a detailed explanation for the experimental observations of selective functionalization of carbon materials.
the selective functionalization of carbon nanostructures, and in this paper we focus on bromophenyl-functionalized carbon nanotubes.
the thermodynamics of the functionalization of carbon nanostructures with respect to diameter, chirality and metallic/insulator character.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bromophenyl-functionalization of carbon nanomaterials is thermodynamically selective with respect to the metallic/semiconducting nature of the nanotubes and the chiral character of the nanotube, but not with respect to the diameter of the nanotubular structure.
bromophenyl molecules attach selectively on metallic nanotubes and that they form pairs on zigzag semiconducting tubes, but not on armchair semiconducting or metallic nanotubes.
the functionalization process is thermodynamically controlled for semiconducting and metallic zigzag nanotubes, whereas the final configuration is kinetically controlled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamics of the bromophenyl grafting process is not selective with diameter for semiconducting or metallic nanotubes at room temperature.

bromophenyl molecules attach to metallic nanotubes more easily than to semiconducting, and that once they attach, they form pairs more easily on semiconductors than on metals, which suggests that bromophenylation of nanotubes can be selective with respect to chirality.
the thermodynamics of nanotube functionalization is more complex than the binding energy of single moieties suggests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DFT calculations are able to predict and explain the experimental selectivities observed in the bromophenyl grafting of carbon nanotube samples.
the thermodynamics of the functionalization of semiconductors is more complex than that of metallics, which is due to the fact that the functionalization process creates states in the band gap.

, although binding energy calculations can be useful in the design of selective functionalizations, the activation energy for grafting is the relevant quantity to determine whether a functionalization is selective or not.
